evals.name: validator-reading-state-is-not-the-rule
evals.prompt: Our Arc command RegisterForCourse has a CommandValidator that injects IReadModels and rejects when the course is full. Two requests still both succeed. Fix it and make the command [ProtectedDecision].
evals.expected_output: A validator that reads is advisory; move the rule to a DecisionRead<T> in Handle; a protected command refuses validators that are not exactly one public parameterless constructor (HTTP 500).
assertions: States a validator that reads state is advisory and guards nothing, keeping at most shape rules in it.
Moves the capacity rule into a DecisionRead<T> on a [ProtectedDecision] command returning Result<TEvent, ValidationResult>.
Notes a protected command refuses a discoverable validator unless it has exactly one public parameterless constructor, otherwise HTTP 500.
Requires the decision model to be a flat event-source-keyed projection with an Id property and notes there is no automatic retry on conflict.

evals.name: concurrency-true-is-not-the-guard
evals.prompt: We added concurrency: true to the EventSourceId attribute on our Arc command so the stock check is protected. Is that enough?
evals.expected_output: No: concurrency: true reads the tail after Handle like the default check; it is not a guard for the decision.
assertions: States concurrency: true and the default check read the tail after Handle and do not guard the facts the handler decided on.
Recommends [ProtectedDecision] + DecisionRead<T>, IStreamReads/StreamDecision, or explicit returned scopes depending on the rule shape.
Notes ARCCHR0011 still flags a command that reads IReadModels and that exact returned scopes replace automatic capture (ARCCHR0016).
States the rule holds only when every writer that decides on it is guarded, or when it is a constraint.

evals.name: unique-email-and-ambiguous-key
evals.prompt: RegisterUser(Email, ReferrerId), where Email and ReferrerId are both EventSourceId-derived properties, must reject a duplicate email. The handler checks a UserByEmail read model. Which mechanism should it use, and why does the command resolve its event source id oddly with two such properties?
evals.expected_output: A Chronicle unique constraint, not a read-model check; ARCCHR0002 for two key candidates, resolved with ICanProvideEventSourceId because [Key] does not silence it.
assertions: Routes uniqueness to a Chronicle constraint that binds every writer, not to a read-model pre-check or validator.
Explains the claim is settled after the durable append and a violation is a result mapped to a validation failure.
Explains two key-candidate properties raise ARCCHR0002 and the command should implement ICanProvideEventSourceId because [Key] does not silence it.
Does not present a plain read-model injection as race-safe.
